headline: Sartorius stake gain lifts profit as revenue holds flat
summary_short: Bio-Rad's Q2 2026 net sales held flat at $651.0M (-0.1% y/y) as 2.6% Clinical Diagnostics growth offset a 4.1% Life Science decline; net income jumped to $371.4M ($13.85/diluted share) mostly on a $458.0M Sartorius AG fair-value gain, while non-GAAP EPS held flat at $2.62.
summary_long: Revenue was essentially flat at $651.0M (-0.1% y/y, -1.9% currency-neutral): Clinical Diagnostics grew 2.6% on quality-systems, diabetes and blood-typing strength, offsetting weaker infectious-disease sales, while Life Science fell 4.1% on academic-research softness, partly offset by >20% digital-PCR growth and an EMEA return to growth. GAAP operating income fell 5.8% y/y to $72.6M; non-GAAP gross margin held near flat at 53.9%. Net income jumped to $371.4M ($13.85/diluted share) almost entirely on a $458.0M fair-value gain in the Sartorius AG stake; non-GAAP EPS was flat at $2.62. Cash plus short-term investments rose to $1,618.5M; the company repurchased ~$32M of shares and reaffirmed FY2026 non-GAAP guidance: revenue -3.0% to +0.5% currency-neutral, operating margin 10.0%-12.0%.

drivers.explanation: Company frames the quarter as flat reported revenue with Clinical Diagnostics growth offsetting Life Science softness; the large GAAP profit swing is a Sartorius AG fair-value mark, not operating improvement; FY2026 outlook reaffirmed unchanged.

Flat total reported revenue: Clinical Diagnostics +2.6% on quality systems, diabetes and blood typing (partly offset by lower infectious-disease sales); Life Science -4.1% on ongoing academic-research market challenges.
Not separately explained in the release; GAAP cost of goods sold was roughly flat y/y ($305.2M vs $306.3M) even as sales were flat, consistent with the near-flat gross margin.
GAAP gross margin ticked up to 53.1% from 53.0% y/y on essentially flat revenue and cost of goods sold; not separately explained beyond the segment mix shift toward Clinical Diagnostics.
y/y decline is arithmetic: flat gross profit against higher SG&A ($212.0M vs $207.7M) partially offset by lower R&D ($61.2M vs $60.5M, essentially flat); not separately explained in the release.
Company attributes the increase to a recognized change in fair market value of its investment in Sartorius AG, which "substantially contributed to a net income" gain this quarter.
Same Sartorius AG fair-value gain drives the swing: GAAP other non-operating line shows a $458.0M favorable change in fair value of equity securities and loan receivable, up from $334.4M a year ago.
Mirrors net income growth on a lower weighted basic share count (26,746K vs 27,226K y/y, down on buybacks); not separately explained in the release.
Mirrors net income growth on a lower weighted diluted share count (26.814M vs 27.228M y/y, down 1.5% on buybacks); not separately explained in the release.
Not separately explained in the release; Q2 free cash flow of $66.7M (operating cash flow $98.7M less $32.0M capex) is the release's own disclosed liquidity generation for the quarter.
Not explained in the release; balance was essentially unchanged q/q and y/y with no debt issuance or repayment activity disclosed.
Not separately explained in the release; consistent with the quarter's net income being largely retained, partially offset by the disclosed ~$32M of share repurchases.
Company states it repurchased approximately $32 million of shares in the quarter, consistent with the lower weighted diluted share count versus both q/q and y/y periods.
